note: Input beginning with '''''' makes the multiline-string scanner match the closing delimiter immediately after advance_n(2), emitting a LEXEME_STRING whose value points at lexer->pos (attacker-controlled input bytes) with len == 0.
The zero-length STRING lexeme is copied into the parser's pending-lexeme buffer as a candidate section name.
The LINEFEED lexeme that follows sees a non-empty pending buffer and routes parsing into shorthand-section parsing.
Shorthand section parsing forwards the buffered lexemes to parse_section().

The section name is appended from a lexeme whose length is zero; the empty lexeme's value pointer is passed without any validity check, so lwan_strbuf_append_str() interprets sz==0 as 'use strlen()' on the pointer.
strlen() walks the zero-length lexeme's value pointer; with a 32768-byte all-non-NUL input the scan runs past the end of the global fuzz buffer, causing a global buffer over-read.
